messages:
sasha: Quick sync — I started a PRD draft for Smart Routing fallback policy. Main goal: reconcile customer-driven asks (ACME, FinBank) with SLA constraints, region/variant compatibility, and rollout gates. Need acceptance criteria and edge-case list before I open the RFC.

anna: Thanks. Can you paste the proposed compatibility matrix and a short example policy here? :eyes:

sasha: Sure — rough matrix below (high-level):

```
# compatibility: model -> compatible fallbacks
redwood-4 => [redwood-3, redwood-2]
redwood-4-quant => [redwood-3-quant, redwood-2-quant]
gpt-qa-13b => [gpt-qa-6b, redwood-3]
```

example policy snippet (proto):
```
policy: {
  tiers: {
    gold: { allow: ["redwood-4","gpt-qa-13b"], fallback: ["redwood-3"], cross_region: false },
    silver: { allow: ["redwood-3"], fallback: ["redwood-2"], cross_region: true }
  }
}
```

mike: +1. A few technical constraints to call out: quantization must preserve tokenizer compatibility and KV cache layout. If tokenizer IDs differ, we must disallow fallback. Edge case: model with identical weights but different tokenizers (happens with forks).

ryan: On SLAs: propose that for gold tier, primary->fallback path must maintain 95th-percentile latency SLO within same region. If only cross-region fallback is possible, mark request as "degraded" and tag response with telemetry, and notify the customer via events.

zara: From FinBank: absolute no cross-region fallbacks for PCI/PHI workloads. We need an opt-out flag at the customer config level and runtime enforcement. Also KMS alignment requirement for Private deployments.

product-lead: Draft acceptance criteria (starting point):
- Policy enforcement: requests are routed according to tier+region+compatibility matrix.
- Safety: incompatible model variants are never routed (tokenizer mismatch, incompatible kv format).
- SLA behavior: gold tier maintains latency SLO for same-region fallbacks; cross-region fallbacks must set degraded flag + emit event.
- Customer controls: per-customer opt-out for cross-region, and per-customer explicit allow-list for fallback variants.
- Observability: metrics + traces for routing decisions (routing.fallback.source, routing.fallback.variant, routing.degraded=true/false).
- Rollout: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated quality checks (see below).

eva: QA plan notes: add an automated diff suite (100 prompts) that runs against primary vs fallback variants. Threshold: <3% regression in task-specific quality metrics (exact metric depends on customer eval set). Performance harness should simulate same-region and cross-region failovers.

mike: Add an edge-case: model aliasing/variant mapping. Example: 'redwood-4' and 'redwood-4-quant' are not automatically compatible even if architecture matches. We need an explicit compatibility mapping table and a validation step at model onboarding.

ryan: Telemetry addition: emit tags routing.fallback.source, routing.fallback.to_variant, routing.fallback.reason. Add an alert for unexpected fallback volume > 1% of total requests for a given customer in 10m.

zara: For Private deployments, enforce KMS key alignment check on fallback variants if data residency is required. Also log an audit entry when a fallback crosses tenant boundaries (should never happen).

deploy-bot: Deployment note: canary job queued with feature flag 'smart-routing-fallback-v2'.

sasha: Next steps: I'll incorporate these acceptance criteria + edge cases into the PRD and add a compatibility checklist for model onboarding. I'll link the doc here once PR created. Please call out any missing customer asks. Meeting to align tomorrow 10:00am PT.

anna: ACK. Add a note for ops runbook: manual override to force-fallback-to-null (for safety).

mike: Also add a failure mode: if fallback itself is failing (5xx), we should degrade to a best-effort cached response (if available) and emit "fallback_failed" event.

product-lead: I'll consolidate and add rollout checklist items (monitoring dashboards, canary thresholds, rollback criteria). Will post PR comments tomorrow.

sasha: Thanks — I will PR EOD and tag @product-lead, @mike, @ryan for review.
